children: KB Home lowered its outlook for housing gross profit margin, as the company is seeing conditions in the housing industry continue to worsen.

The homebuilder said Tuesday it now expects annual gross profit margin to be 16.0% to 16.2%, down from its earlier guidance of 16.1% to 16.5%. It now expects housing revenue to be $4.9 billion to $5.1 billion, compared with its earlier range of $4.9 billion to $5.3 billion.
Its projection for annual home deliveries remained the same, at 10,500 to 11,000 homes.
"When we provided margin guidance on our last call, our outlook for the fourth quarter was more favorable than it is today," Chief Accounting Officer Bill Hollinger said.

Conditions in the housing market have weakened since KB Home's June earnings report, executives said. High mortgage rates, pressure on housing affordability and geopolitical uncertainty are all weighing on the industry, they said.

In the fiscal third quarter, KB Home's revenue fell 20%, to $1.3 billion, in line with what analysts forecasted. The number of homes delivered decreased 19%, to 2,732, and net orders were down 12%, to 2,604.
Sales in June were resilient and slightly ahead of May, but they softened sequentially in July and August. That resulted in the year-over-year decline in orders, executives said.
Profit decreased to $65.3 million, or $1.05 a share, from $109.8 million, or $1.61 a share, a year earlier.

The lower margin guidance is due to the fact that the current fourth quarter is looking less promising than executives originally thought, Hollinger said. Management now expects a smaller contribution from higher margin communities on the West Coast, primarily due to worse conditions in Southern California.

In the fourth quarter, KB Home anticipates housing revenue of $1.45 billion to $1.65 billion, with 3,000 to 3,500 homes delivered. Analysts were guiding for $1.63 billion in housing sales and about 3,244 homes delivered.

Southern California had slower-than-expected sales in the third quarter, which has reduced the number of higher-priced homes the company expects to close in the fourth quarter. KB Home has also lowered some prices in response to market conditions and higher mortgage rates, Hollinger said.
"More broadly, softer market conditions and greater affordability pressures have contributed to increased pricing pressures across many of our markets," he said.
KB Home's average selling price decreased to $473,000 from $475,700 in the latest quarter.

Earlier this month, Lennar cut its home-delivery target for the full year, citing interest-rate pressure and worsening conditions in the housing market. Low consumer confidence, high home prices and the Federal Reserve's recent interest-rate boost were all weighing on new home projections, the homebuilder said.

The Fed this month raised interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point, bringing the average daily mortgage rates above 7% for 30-year fixed rate loans. Economists expect the milestone of 7% to further spook buyers in an already stagnant market.
